desc:
A matrix is diagonal-constant (a Toeplitz matrix) when every diagonal that runs from the top-left towards the bottom-right holds a single repeated value. Given a rows × cols matrix, return true if it has this property and false otherwise.

Equivalently, matrix[i][j] equals matrix[i + 1][j + 1] whenever both cells exist.

[[1, 2, 3, 4],
 [5, 1, 2, 3],
 [9, 5, 1, 2]]  →  true

[[1, 2],
 [2, 2]]  →  false
hints: Cells on the same top-left to bottom-right diagonal have the same value of i - j.
You do not need to group diagonals. It is enough to compare neighbouring cells along each diagonal.
Check every cell that has a cell above-left of it: it must equal matrix[i - 1][j - 1]. If all of those comparisons hold, every diagonal is constant.
editorial: Each diagonal is a chain of cells (i, j), (i + 1, j + 1), (i + 2, j + 2), .... A chain is constant exactly when every consecutive pair is equal, so it is enough to verify matrix[i][j] == matrix[i - 1][j - 1] for all i, j ≥ 1.
That is a single scan over the matrix: O(rows · cols) time and O(1) extra space. A hash map from i - j to the first value seen on that diagonal also works but needs extra memory.
